subject: thorny devil lizard
title: This Desert Lizard Drinks Through Its Skin, Not Its Mouth

scenes.text: This lizard can drink without ever touching water to its mouth.
It lives in the Australian desert, where rain can miss it for months.
So the thorny devil's whole body works like a sponge. Dew or damp sand touches its skin, and the water spreads out.
Tiny channels between its overlapping scales act like drinking straws, pulling the water across its body.
No pumping. No sipping. Physics does the work, and the water ends up at its mouth.
The driest place it lives, and the lizard is wearing its own water pipes.

description:
The thorny devil of the Australian desert can collect water with its skin.
Tiny channels between its overlapping scales draw water by capillary action toward its mouth, a system a 2017 study in Royal Society Open Science examined.
What other desert animal do you think has the wildest survival trick?
